correctness.rationale: For \(k\ge2\) nonzero diagonals, completing the square reduces each x-slice to a nondegenerate binary quadratic form or a single square. The quadratic-character count and a separate count for d=0 determine every nonzero determinant fiber. For k=1 and k=0, multiplicative pair counting applies directly. Summing over nonzero determinants and using the quadratic-character identity yields exact zero-fiber sizes. The proof is uniform for all odd prime powers, and 1,911,396 independently enumerated matrices verify 17,820 fibers in the named finite cases; finite checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: Four targeted mathematical-record searches and primary-literature comparisons revealed no exact conditional determinant-fiber formula for all three fixed diagonal entries of a symmetric 3-by-3 matrix over odd fields. The distinct full-matrix result of Gorodetsky, the general-linear Gauss transforms of Li–Hu, and unconditional symmetric determinant counts of Brent–McKay cannot by their stated conclusions recover the conditional fibers. Hodges (1955) remains a material unresolved priority risk; no independent originality certification is asserted.

value.rationale: A fully motivated conditional arithmetic invariant of a classical finite-field object receives a complete exact natural classification, including its nontrivial quadratic-character dependence and the surprising support-only law for singular matrices. It resolves all field sizes in odd characteristic and every possible fixed diagonal for the first cubic determinant hypersurface, rather than an arbitrary unmotivated subcase or existing unconditional table.
